title: Converting and packaging
summary: PEM, DER and PFX conversions with openssl and certutil, matching a key to a certificate, and Java keystores with keytool.

steps.title: Conversions you will need
body: | PEM → DER | `openssl x509 -in cert.pem -outform DER -out cert.der` | `certutil -decode cert.pem cert.der` |
| DER → PEM | `openssl x509 -inform DER -in cert.der -out cert.pem` | `certutil -encode cert.der cert.pem` |
| key + cert (+ chain) → PFX | `openssl pkcs12 -export -inkey key.pem -in cert.pem -certfile int.pem -out site.pfx` | `Export-PfxCertificate` |
| PFX → certificates | `openssl pkcs12 -in site.pfx -nokeys -out certs.pem` | `certutil -dump site.pfx` to look |
| PFX → private key | `openssl pkcs12 -in site.pfx -nocerts -noenc -out key.pem` | |
| .p7b → PEM | `openssl pkcs7 -in chain.p7b -print_certs -out chain.pem` | open it, export each |
- `-noenc` (older: `-nodes`) writes the key **unencrypted**. Protect that file (`chmod 600`).

- **OpenSSL 3 and old PFX files:** PFX files from older Windows and Java use RC2/3DES. OpenSSL 3 refuses them (`error:0308010C:digital envelope routines::unsupported`) until you add **`-legacy`**. To *make* a PFX for an old system, add `-legacy` to `pkcs12 -export` as well.

steps.prompt: Match each command to what it produces.
pairs: a password-protected bundle of key and certificate
the certificates from a PFX, as PEM
the unencrypted private key from a PFX

steps.prompt: Bundle a key, its certificate and the intermediate into a PFX, then pull only the certificates back out.
code: openssl pkcs12 __1__ -inkey key.pem -in cert.pem __2__ int.pem -out site.pfx
steps.explain: `-export` creates a PFX; without it `pkcs12` reads one. `-certfile` adds extra certificates (the chain). `-nokeys` leaves the key out.

steps.prompt: OpenSSL 3 fails to open a PFX exported years ago from Windows Server 2012. Which flag do you add? Type just the flag.
steps.explain: RC2-40 lives in OpenSSL 3's legacy provider. `-legacy` loads it. Better still, re-export the PFX with AES (`openssl pkcs12 -export` defaults to AES-256 in OpenSSL 3).

steps.title: Does this key belong to this certificate?
body: nginx says `SSL_CTX_use_PrivateKey ... key values mismatch`; IIS imports a certificate with no key. Check by comparing the **public key** inside both files:
# any key type (RSA, EC): hash the public key from each side
Same hash: they belong together. In .NET, compare `cert.PublicKey.ExportSubjectPublicKeyInfo()` with `key.ExportSubjectPublicKeyInfo()`.
keytool -importcert -cacerts -alias dojo-root -file root.pem      # the JDK's own cacerts (password changeit)

steps.prompt: You run both public-key hashes and get two **different** values. What does it mean?
options: The key does not belong to the certificate: find the right key, or issue a new certificate for this key
One file is DER and the other PEM
steps.explain: The certificate binds exactly one public key. A different hash means a different key pair, whatever the file names say.

steps.prompt: Can the file contain a private key?
steps.explain: PKCS#12 and Java keystores can hold keys; .cer, .der, .p7b and a fullchain never do. A `.pem` can hold anything: look for `BEGIN PRIVATE KEY`.

code: static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);
steps.explain: DER certificates start with `0x30` (an ASN.1 SEQUENCE). PEM is the same bytes in Base64 between BEGIN/END lines, so converting back gives identical bytes.

steps.title: PEM to DER by hand
prompt: Write `byte[] PemToDer(string pem)`: what `openssl x509 -outform DER` and `certutil -decode` do.

Take the text between `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----` and `-----END CERTIFICATE-----`, remove the line breaks (the input may use `\n` or `\r\n`), and Base64-decode it. If there are several certificates, return only the first. Text before the BEGIN line (like `subject=...` from openssl) must be ignored.
Do it by hand: no `PemEncoding`, `ImportFromPem` or `CreateFromPem`.
hints: `pem.IndexOf(end, start)` finds the END after the first BEGIN.
template:
Dojo.Eq("text before the PEM is ignored, first of two wins", dojoA.RawData, PemToDer("subject=CN = a.example
issuer=CN = a.example
" + dojoA.ExportCertificatePem() + "
" + dojoB.ExportCertificatePem()));
static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);

steps.title: Does the key match the certificate?
prompt: Write `bool KeyMatches(X509Certificate2 cert, ECDsa key)`, the .NET version of comparing `openssl x509 -pubkey` with `openssl pkey -pubout`: compare the certificate's SubjectPublicKeyInfo bytes with the key's.
Return `false` (don't throw) when the certificate's key is not an ECDSA key at all.
template: var dojoReq = new CertificateRequest("CN=match.example", dojoKey, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
Dojo.Eq("the right key matches", true, KeyMatches(dojoPublic, dojoKey));
Dojo.Eq("another key does not", false, KeyMatches(dojoPublic, dojoOtherKey));

using var dojoRsaCert = new CertificateRequest("CN=rsa.example", dojoRsa, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256, RSASignaturePadding.Pkcs1).CreateSelfSigned(DateTimeOffset.UnixEpoch, DateTimeOffset.UnixEpoch.AddYears(1));
Dojo.Eq("an RSA certificate never matches an EC key", false, KeyMatches(dojoRsaCert, dojoKey));

if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
